claim: A consumer's mbarrier parity wait for Stage i, phase p returns only after the elected producer's single arrival and all transaction bytes tracked for the TMA copy have completed; issuing the copy alone is not sufficient.
question: Which native TMA and mbarrier events must occur before a consumer warpgroup's parity wait lets it read a shared-memory stage?
audience: CUDA developers learning Hopper TMA and asynchronous transaction barriers
scope: One elected producer thread contributes the single software arrival and expected transaction bytes for one TMA global-to-shared copy; consumer threads use an mbarrier parity wait for the same shared-memory phase. Source preparation, proxy handoff details, TensorMap construction, and exact copy latency remain outside the sequence.
readingOrder: Read top to bottom: the elected producer contributes one arrival, registers expected transaction bytes for Stage i, phase p, and issues the TMA copy; consumers may call try_wait_parity(p), but the matching wait returns only after that arrival and all tracked transaction bytes are complete.
